expo.name: Hybrid Engine
expo.//owner: The project lives under the ths1s-team ORGANISATION, not a personal account. Without this, EAS resolves the build against whichever account the token belongs to and fails to find the project.
expo.//runtimeVersion: A FIXED STRING, deliberately not the 'fingerprint' policy. Fingerprint hashes the autolinked native module directories, and under pnpm those directory names embed the peer-resolution hash — so adding eas-cli to the workspace injected 'graphql@16.8.1' into every expo-* path and silently changed the runtime version. Updates then published under a version no installed app had, and every phone correctly ignored them, with no error anywhere. BUMP THIS BY HAND, in the same commit as any NATIVE change (new native module, new permission, icon, Expo SDK bump), and ship a fresh APK with it. Never bump it for a JS-only change — that is exactly what lets those ship over the air.
expo.//runtimeVersion-3: Bumped 2 -> 3 for expo-camera: a new native module (CameraX + ML Kit barcode-scanning) and a new CAMERA permission. Both are NATIVE changes, so no phone on runtime 2 can run this JS and every one of them must get a fresh APK. This is exactly the bump the note above demands.
expo.//runtimeVersion-4: Bumped 3 -> 4 for expo-mlkit-ocr: the label reader now photographs a nutrition panel and recognises it on-device via com.google.mlkit:text-recognition. That is a NEW NATIVE MODULE with its own Android artifact, so it cannot travel over the air — a runtime-3 phone given this JS would resolve ExpoMlkitOcr to nothing. No new permission: CAMERA was already declared for the barcode scanner. Ship a fresh APK with this. The screen still degrades to typed entry if the module is absent, but that is a seatbelt, not a substitute for the bump.

updates.//: u.expo.dev/<projectId> is EAS Update's fixed URL shape — same projectId as extra.eas below.

android.//: applicationId, versionCode and the signing keystore must match the existing native/android-app build or Play treats this as a NEW app and current users get a second icon instead of an update.

adaptiveIcon.//: Reproduces the SHIPPED launcher exactly: native/android-app inset ic_raw 18% on a #080808 field. Change it and every existing user watches their icon change during what is supposed to be a silent update.

infoPlist.NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription: Connects to your heart-rate strap so conditioning can be run by heart rate.
infoPlist.NSMotionUsageDescription: Reads the phone's step counter for daily activity.
infoPlist.NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription: Tracks your route and pace during outdoor conditioning.
infoPlist.NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescrip: Tracks your route and pace during outdoor conditioning, including with the screen locked.

plugins.bluetoothAlwaysPermission: Connects to your heart-rate strap so conditioning can be run by heart rate.

plugins.locationAlwaysAndWhenInUsePermission: Tracks your route and pace during outdoor conditioning, including with the screen locked.
plugins.locationWhenInUsePermission: Tracks your route and pace during outdoor conditioning.

plugins.//: Barcode scanning only. Microphone and the media library are explicitly disabled so prebuild does not add RECORD_AUDIO or storage permissions the app has no use for — Play asks about every one of them.
plugins.cameraPermission: Scans a food barcode, or photographs a nutrition panel, so a food can be looked up or read. Images are read on this phone and never uploaded or saved.

plugins.//: On-device text recognition for the nutrition-label reader. Android autolinking comes from the package's own expo-module.config.json and needs nothing here; this entry exists for the config plugin, whose ONLY effect is an iOS Podfile post_install that stops ML Kit's arm64 simulator gap breaking a pod install. It touches no Android file, adds no permission and no manifest entry, which is why it is listed with its default props rather than configured.

eas.//: The EAS project this app builds under. `eas init --id` writes exactly this; it is recorded here rather than run because CI builds are --non-interactive and cannot be prompted to link a project mid-build. Not a secret: it identifies the project, it does not grant access to it. That is EXPO_TOKEN, which lives in GitHub secrets.
